answer: Persistent identity handoff: each agent identity must inherit a live session context from an existing verified agent, transferring a rotating opal token that only one holder can use at a time. A new identity requires a sponsor to surrender its active token for a full cycle, during which the sponsor cannot transact. This lantern constraint makes mass registration costly: an attacker must idle real productive agents for each fake identity created. A beacon check confirms token lineage at each transaction. The per-identity cost is lost operational capacity, not capital.
